Sunil Kumar Baid Huf vs Union Of India & Anr on 11 August,
2023
Author: Bibek Chaudhuri

Bench: Bibek Chaudhuri
11.08.2023
 Sl. No.08.
 Mithun
 Ct.No.42.
 Wpa 18122 of 2023
 Sunil Kumar Baid Huf
 Vs.
 Union of India & Anr.
 Mr. Ayan Banerjee,
 Mr. Suman Banerjee,
 ...for the petitioner.
By a Gazette Notification under Section 10 of the  Metro Railways (Construction of Works) Act, 1978 dated  2nd September, 2020, a declaration of acquisition of  petitioner's land was published.
Subsequently an order  under Section 13 of the said Act was passed declaring  the compensation payable to the petitioner.
Being an  aggrieved against the amount of compensation, the  petitioner moved the Tribunal praying for enhancement  of compensation.
The competent authority passed an  order enhancing the compensation amount.
Against the  said order both the petitioner and the Metro Railways  preferred appeals before the Tribunal.

The Tribunal  dismissed the appeal filed by the Metro Railways and  allowed the appeal filed by the petitioner further Sunil Kumar Baid Huf vs Union Of India & Anr on 11 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189931069/
1  enhancing the compensation.

sentences.text: However, without  depositing the compensation amount the Metro Railways  took over the possession of the acquired land and fixed a  2 board thereon.

It is also alleged by the petitioner that the petitioner though entitle to interest on compensation under Section 80 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, no interest has either been calculated or deposited by the respondents.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In spite of affidavit of service, the respondents remained absent.
Considering the case of the petitioner made in the instant writ petition, this writ petition is required to be heard on merit.
Under such circumstances, the respondents are directed to submit a report in the form of affidavit within three weeks from the date of this order.
The petitioner is at liberty to pray for interim order before the Regular Bench upon notice to the respondents.
